sections.title: Detailed Brief Overview
rows: The study of plant function, including **Photosynthesis**, **Respiration**, **Transpiration**, and **Plant Hormones**.
Conversion of solar energy into chemical energy via **Chlorophyll** and **Stomata** mechanisms.
Water absorption through the **Root** and loss through **Leaf** transpiration channels.
UPSSSC PET (Preliminary Eligibility Test) General Science section.
**Chloroplasts** for photosynthesis and **Mitochondria** for cellular respiration.
Macro and Micro-nutrients essential for metabolic pathways in plants.
High-yield direct factual questions on hormones, pigment names, and gas exchange.
Enzyme-driven biochemical reactions maintaining plant life cycle and growth.

items.title: 1. Photosynthesis & Chlorophyll Mechanics
items.content:
• Process by which green plants manufacture food using **sunlight**, **carbon dioxide**, and **water**.
• Occurs inside **Chloroplasts** containing the green pigment **Chlorophyll**.
• **Light Reaction (Thylakoid):** Photolysis of water releases oxygen and generates **ATP** and **NADPH**.
• **Dark Reaction/Calvin Cycle (Stroma):** Fixation of $CO_2$ into glucose without direct light.
• **Mnemonic for Phases:** **'L'ight in 'T'he 'S'un, 'D'ark in 'S'troma** (Light-Thylakoid-Sun, Dark-Stroma).

items.title: 2. Respiration & Energy Currency
items.content:
• Breakdown of complex organic molecules to release energy in living cells.
• Occurs continuously in both light and dark conditions.
• **Glycolysis:** Takes place in the **cytoplasm** (glucose broken down to pyruvate).
• **Krebs Cycle & ETS:** Takes place in the **mitochondria**.
• Energy released is stored as **ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate)**.
• **Mnemonic for Aerobic Steps:** **'G'et 'K'eys 'E'arly** (Glycolysis -> Krebs Cycle -> Electron Transport System).

items.title: 3. Transpiration & Stomatal Regulation
items.content:
• Loss of water in the form of water vapor from aerial parts of the plant.
• Regulated by microscopic pores called **Stomata** present mostly on the **Leaf** surface.
• Guard cells control the opening and closing of **stomata** based on turgor pressure and **potassium ion ($K^+$)** influx.
• Creates a suction pull (transpiration pull) that helps in the ascent of sap from the **Root**.
• **Mnemonic for Stomatal Opening:** **'K'eys 'O'pen 'W'ater** ($K^+$ influx leads to osmotic water entry and opening).

items.title: 4. Plant Growth Regulators (Plant Hormones)
items.content:
• Chemical messengers that regulate growth, development, and responses to stimuli.
• **Auxins:** Promotes cell elongation, apical dominance (**F.W. Went** discovery).
• **Gibberellins (GA):** Stem elongation, seed germination, bolting (**Kurosawa** discovery).
• **Cytokinins:** Promotes cell division, delays leaf senescence.
• **Ethylene:** Gaseous hormone, fruit ripening (**Gane** discovery).
• **Abscisic Acid (ABA):** Stress hormone, promotes stomatal closure and seed dormancy.
• **Mnemonic for Hormones:** **'A'll 'G'reen 'C'orn 'E'at 'A'pples** (Auxin, Gibberellin, Cytokinin, Ethylene, Abscisic Acid).

items.title: 5. Root Absorption & Mineral Nutrition
items.content:
• Roots absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil via **osmosis** and **active transport**.
• **Xylem** tissue transports water and minerals upward from the **Root** to the **Leaf**.
• **Phloem** tissue transports synthesized food (organic solutes) bidirectionally.
• Essential elements divided into macronutrients (e.g., Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium) and micronutrients (e.g., Iron, Zinc, Boron).
• **Mnemonic for Macronutrients:** **'C. H. O. N. P. K. Ca. Mg. S.'** (Carbon, Hydrogen, Oxygen, Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, Sulfur).

items.definition: Remember **X**ylem goes **UP** (Water & minerals unidirectionally); **P**hloem goes **ANYWHERE** (Food bidirectional).
Remember **Thylakoid** starts with **T** (Thylakoid = **T**raffic light for photosynthesis light reaction).
Remember **Stroma** contains **S** (Stroma = **S**unless region for dark reaction).
Remember **Ethylene** is a gas because it ends in **-ene** like alkene gases in chemistry.
Remember **Abscisic Acid** acts during **A**bsence of water / **A**larm conditions (Stress hormone).
Remember **Magnesium** is the green center of plant life (**M**agnesium = **M**agnet for sunlight in chlorophyll).

items.term: Mistake 1: Confusing Xylem and Phloem Functions
items.definition: Students often think phloem transports water. **Correction:** Xylem transports water and minerals; Phloem transports food/organic solutes.
Students think released oxygen comes from $CO_2$. **Correction:** Oxygen released during photosynthesis comes from the **photolysis of water ($H_2O$)**.
Students confuse plant breathing with cellular respiration. **Correction:** Respiration is a biochemical oxidation process occurring inside cells, not just gas exchange.
Students mix up Cytokinin and Auxin functions. **Correction:** Auxin promotes apical dominance and cell elongation; Cytokinin promotes lateral bud growth and cell division.
Students think water loss causes stomata to open. **Correction:** Influx of $K^+$ ions draws water in, increasing turgor pressure to **open** stomata.
Students confuse Iron with Magnesium in chlorophyll. **Correction:** Chlorophyll has a **Magnesium ($Mg$)** core, whereas Hemoglobin has an **Iron ($Fe$)** core.
An anabolic, endergonic process converting light energy into chemical energy inside **chloroplasts**.
**Chlorophyll** absorbs blue and red wavelengths of light and reflects green light.
Splitting of water molecules during the light reaction, releasing electrons, protons, and **oxygen**.
Biochemical pathway occurring in the **stroma** where $CO_2$ is fixed into hexose sugars.
Catabolic process breaking down glucose to release **ATP** energy in the mitochondria.
Influenced by temperature, light intensity, humidity, wind speed, and **stomata** distribution.
Positive pressure developed in **roots** that helps push water up to small heights in herbaceous plants.
Discovered by **F.W. Went** using oat coleoptiles; responsible for phototropic bending.
Induces stem elongation and breaks dormancy in seeds and buds.
Works synergistically with auxin to stimulate cell division (**cytokinesis**).
Commercial ripening agent for bananas, mangoes, and tomatoes; induces flowering in pineapples.
Known as the stress hormone; induces stomatal closure during drought stress.

upscNotes.content: UPSSSC PET frequently asks direct match-the-following questions on Plant Hormones and their discoverers or primary functions. Memorize the exact hormone names.
Focus heavily on the chemical equation of photosynthesis and respiration, particularly identifying the source of oxygen gas released.
Trap: Students often select Iron ($Fe$) when asked about the central metal ion in chlorophyll. The correct answer is Magnesium ($Mg$). Iron is present in cytochromes and ferredoxin.
Trap: Ethylene is the only gaseous plant hormone. Do not confuse it with Abscisic acid or Cytokinin when asked about fruit ripening.

keyTakeaways: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy inside chloroplasts containing **chlorophyll**.
Respiration breaks down glucose to release **ATP** energy in the mitochondria.
Transpiration regulates water balance through **stomata** located on the **leaf** surface.
Water and minerals are transported upward by **xylem** originating from the **root**.
Plant hormones like **Auxin**, **Gibberellin**, **Cytokinin**, **Ethylene**, and **Abscisic Acid** control growth and development.
The central metal atom of the chlorophyll molecule is **Magnesium ($Mg$)**.
